data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 asserts decentralized heterogeneity prevents SPOF-trigger propagation and bypasses internal redundancy, but it supplies no causal mechanism for WHY operators actually remain heterogeneous. The problem demands a causal mechanism distinguishing independent vs. merely-uncorrelated failures. Its own counterconditions (common upstream dependency; convergence on industry-best stack) concede the mechanism can collapse, yet the claim and mechanism offer no account of the stabilizing forces that sustain heterogeneity in the first place—nor of how to tell, observationally, whether apparent independence rests on genuine diversity vs. a hidden shared layer not yet triggered. Without that, the 'fragmentation firewall' is an asserted effect with no demonstrated cause.
